# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*Objective: Draw a single continuous closed loop through the grid*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Connect dots with lines; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles have different turn rules

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
- **Nagareru** — Loop travels through cells; directional wind constraints force movement
- **Suraromu** — Loop passes through numbered "Gates" in a specific order
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop traverses rooms alternating between moon and sun cells
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through black circles at their midpoints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

#### 1.3 Constrained Circle/Region Loop
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-bordered area, all circles must be either all straight or all turning
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing lines (open-ended paths, not closed loop)

---

### 2. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*Objective: Color or blacken specific cells according to constraints*

#### 2.1 Shading with Connectivity Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected wall; numbered white islands of exact size
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in rooms; no two shaded cells touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row or column; shaded cells cannot touch
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells; numbers indicate total visible white cells horizontally and vertically
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; numbers in circles indicate sum of adjacent continuous black cell groups
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; numbers indicate adjacent shaded cells but one number per bold region is deliberately wrong

#### 2.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Shaded regions must be rectangular; white regions must be non-rectangular
- **LITS** — Shade exactly four cells (tetromino) per bold region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of shaded cells) so each bold region contains exactly two shaded cells
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains exactly two same-sized shading blocks; all shading connected globally
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half

#### 2.3 Shading with Visual/Maze Output
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles off it
- **Tilepaint** — Shade whole tiles; diagonal-numbered cells constrain counts; solution outlines an object
- **Shakashaka** — Place half-cell triangles so remaining white areas form only rectangles/squares

---

### 3. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Fill cells with numbers satisfying given constraints*

#### 3.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block exactly once
- **Hitori** — (Also shading) No number repeated in any row or column

#### 3.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers; each number defines a region of that many cells; same-size regions cannot touch
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold room contains 1 through N; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow-black-cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in different rooms cannot be adjacent

#### 3.3 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with numbers from a given list; numbers run horizontally or vertically

---

### 4. REGION-DIVISION GAMES
*Objective: Partition the grid into regions satisfying shape or size rules*

#### 4.1 Division into Uniform Rectangles
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

#### 4.2 Division into Uniform Non-Rectangular Shapes
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

#### 4.3 Division into Matched Pairs
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white sub-region and a gray sub-region of identical shape
- **Chained Block** — Fill black cells into blocks; blocks touch corner-to-corner in chains; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

---

### 5. PATH / MOVEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Move or connect elements through the grid along constrained paths*

#### 5.1 Circle/Piece Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home country; numbered circles move exact distances; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths cannot cross; gray area totals must match

#### 5.2 Sequential Snake Placement
- **Hebi** — Place numbered snake segments (1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch; directional line-of-sight attack rules apply

#### 5.3 Bridge/Connection Building
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered island circles with bridges; bridge count matches island number; all islands connected

---

### 6. EVOLVING / SEQUENTIAL STRUCTURE GAMES
*Objective: Build structures that grow or evolve according to ordered rules*

- **Evolomino** — Place squares in cells; groups form blocks on arrows; each successive block along an arrow adds one square to the previous shape
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight strips with a tip); draw lines from tips through a number of cells matching the pencil's number

---

### 7. SYMBOL-FILLING GAMES
*Objective: Fill cells with non-numeric symbols satisfying directional or regional constraints*

- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with "—" or "|"; territories have counts of each; horizontal runs limited vertically, vertical runs limited horizontally

---

### 8. LIGHT / VISIBILITY GAMES
*Objective: Place elements so that visibility or illumination constraints are satisfied*

- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count

---

## Cross-Cutting Structural Properties

| Property | Games |
|---|---|
| **Uses bold-bordered regions/rooms** | Heyawake, Fillomino, Double Choco, Ripple Effect, Makaro, LITS, Norinori, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Chained Block, Juosan, Nurimisaki, Sashigane, Five Cells |
| **Requires global connectivity** | Nurikabe, Hitori, Kurodoko, Heyawake, Usowan, Nurimisaki, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Prohibits 2×2 filled squares** | Nurikabe, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin |
| **Single closed loop output** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Nagareru, Suraromu, Moon-or-Sun, Mid-loop, Yajilin, Dotchi-Loop |
| **Arrow/directional clues** | Yajilin, Sashigane, Makaro, Hebi, Yosenabe, Evolomino, Nagareru |
| **Solution depicts an image** | Tilepaint |
